summary: Dedicated: Elevated p99 latency + intermittent 5xx on us-east pool (llama-3.1-70b-instruct) impacting production traffic
description:
Issue summary
Customer (AsterIQ) reports elevated p99 latency and intermittent 5xx errors on their Dedicated pool in us-east.

Impact
- Customer observed p99 latency increasing from ~750–900ms baseline to 2.1–3.0s for ~35–50 minutes.
- Intermittent 5xx (HTTP 502/503) bursts during the same window. Customer estimates 0.6–1.3% request failure for affected period.
- Production traffic impacted; customer is concerned this violates Dedicated tier reliability expectations.

Customer context
- Tier: Dedicated capacity (single-tenant pool)
- Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions (streaming enabled)
- Model: llama-3.1-70b-instruct (pinned)
- Region: us-east

Time window (customer-provided)
- 2026-02-03 18:05–18:55 UTC (peak impact around 18:20–18:40 UTC)

Evidence / examples
- Request IDs (gateway):
  - req_01HS2J8M8C4K2Y1Y9V8N6H2R5F (502 at 18:27:11 UTC)
  - req_01HS2JB2F7P1M3N9Q0T6X1V2AA (p99-like latency reported ~2.8s at 18:33:04 UTC)
  - req_01HS2JCNK3D6J2B4Q7E9P0L1ZZ (503 at 18:38:55 UTC)

Initial hypothesis (Support)
Given Dedicated pool isolation, suspect capacity/queueing behavior (autoscaling lag, scheduler saturation, node health flap) rather than shared-hosted noisy neighbor. Request escalation to SRE + Dedicated readiness signal owners.

Customer question (explicit)
- "What are our Dedicated SLO targets for latency/availability, and what do you do operationally when they’re at risk?"
(Also see SUP-3950 where customer requested documented SLOs; linking here for continuity.)
comments: 2026-02-03 19:02 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Acknowledged receipt to customer and requested (a) exact model pin/version string, (b) whether streaming disconnects were observed, (c) approx RPS during window, (d) 3–5 failing request IDs. Opened INC-2026-02-03-us-east-ded-p99 and paged SRE oncall per Dedicated escalation policy.

2026-02-03 19:10 UTC — Rachel Kim (Enterprise Comms): Noted customer is on Enterprise/Dedicated with weekly exec review. Asked to include clear explanation of Dedicated SLO expectations + mitigation steps in the next update.

2026-02-03 19:18 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE): Taking point. Pulled gateway metrics for tenant asteriq-prod, region us-east. Confirmed elevated tail latency (p99) on chat streaming and correlated 5xx spikes (primarily 503 from upstream). Starting deeper dive into scheduler queue depth + node health events.

2026-02-03 19:31 UTC — Vanessa Ortiz (Dedicated readiness): Seeing readiness dips in us-east dedicated cluster around 18:22–18:41 UTC (scheduler health signal intermittent). This looks like capacity signal flapping rather than model/runtime crash-loop. Will check recent node maintenance/drain events.

2026-02-03 19:47 UTC — Mina Haddad (Routing): For Dedicated pools, routing is pinned to the tenant pool; no cross-tier fallback. However, we do have intra-pool replica selection. If scheduler health is flapping, gateway can see 503s depending on upstream selection and retry behavior. Checking for retry amplification at the gateway.

2026-02-03 20:05 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE): Preliminary finding: autoscaler lag + partial GPU node drain in the dedicated pool led to transient under-provisioning. Queue depth rose, driving p99. During the drain, some requests were routed to replicas failing readiness checks, returning 503. Requesting infra logs for drain event IDs.

2026-02-03 20:22 UTC — Logan Wright (Telemetry): Confirmed metrics alignment: 5xx spike is real (not a logging artifact). Notably, gateway shows 503 rate up; runtime 5xx stable → implies upstream selection/availability rather than runtime internal error. Linking dashboards in incident channel #incidents (INC-2026-02-03-us-east-ded-p99).

2026-02-03 20:55 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Sent customer interim update: we’ve confirmed elevated p99 and upstream 503 bursts in the window; active investigation is focused on dedicated pool readiness/capacity event. ETA next update in 60 minutes. Asked customer to share their client-side timeout configuration to rule out aggressive timeouts contributing to retries.

2026-02-03 21:34 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE): Root cause: GPU node drain + readiness propagation lag. During drain, scheduler marked some capacity unavailable; gateway still had a small window where it considered targets healthy, leading to 503s. Retry policy increased load briefly (amplified queueing). Mitigation applied: increased min warm capacity for this tenant pool (+2 replicas) and temporarily tightened gateway upstream selection to require fresh readiness heartbeat.

2026-02-04 00:12 UTC — Ethan Park (Control Plane): Confirmed this is consistent with known gap in dedicated readiness SLI emission + alerting; aligns with ENG-2419/ENG-2420 work. We should track this incident as validation for dedicated pool readiness SLO + alerts.

2026-02-04 10:05 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Customer asked whether this counts against Dedicated SLO and what the expected targets are. I referenced the draft tiered SLO definitions page (internal) and explained we are formalizing tiered SLOs/error budgets; for now, we will provide a customer-specific summary of observed availability/latency during the impacted window and mitigations to reduce recurrence. Requested permission to share a redacted timeline.

2026-02-04 17:20 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE): Monitoring shows p99 returned to baseline (sub-1s) and 5xx back to normal (<0.05%) after mitigation. No further readiness dips since capacity floor change. Proposed follow-ups: (1) ship dedicated readiness SLI improvements (see redwood/pull_request_18474), (2) update alert payloads/runbooks to include readiness + queue depth for dedicated pools (see redwood/pull_request_18489), (3) confirm retry policy guardrails for dedicated upstream selection.

2026-02-05 15:48 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Sent customer final update: confirmed cause was transient capacity reduction due to planned node drain + lag in readiness propagation; mitigated by raising minimum warm capacity and tightening readiness gating for upstream selection. Shared that cross-tier fallback does not apply to Dedicated (to preserve isolation), but we can improve readiness signals and scheduling during maintenance. Offered post-incident review call with SRE + Dedicated PM.

2026-02-07 09:12 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Customer confirmed stability over the weekend and accepted resolution. Closing ticket; leaving linked follow-ups in engineering backlog via ENG-2419/ENG-2420 and keeping SUP-3950 open for the documented SLOs request.
resolution:
Resolved on 2026-02-07 after mitigation and customer confirmation.

Mitigation/changes applied
- Increased minimum warm capacity for AsterIQ dedicated pool in us-east to reduce autoscaler lag sensitivity.
- Tightened gateway upstream selection to require fresh readiness heartbeat during/after node drains.
- Added internal monitoring focus on dedicated scheduler health + queue depth for this tenant.

Notes on Dedicated SLO expectations
- Dedicated SLO definitions are being finalized and published internally (tiered SLO definitions + dedicated readiness notes). Customer-facing SLA terms are unchanged; however, support will provide transparent incident timelines and the operational behaviors we take when SLOs are at risk.

Follow-ups
- Improve dedicated pool readiness SLI emission + dashboarding (redwood/pull_request_18474).
- Improve oncall alert payloads/runbook linkage for dedicated readiness incidents (redwood/pull_request_18489).
- Validate retry policy/guardrails for dedicated upstream selection during maintenance windows (owned by API gateway + routing; track via ENG initiative).
